simple.meaning: חַטִּיל (Chaṭṭîyl) is a Hebrew word meaning “Chattil , one of 'Solomon's servants'.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חַטִּיל (H2411) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 2:57, with occurrences in Ezra, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חַטִּיל (H2411) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חַטִּיל (H2411) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חַטִּיל (Chaṭṭîyl) / H2411 is traced through Ezra 2:57, Nehemiah 7:59 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2411. Chattil חַטִּיל proper name, masculine head of a family of 'the children of Solomon's servants' Ezra 2:57 ᵐ5 Αττεια , A Αττιλ = Neh 7:59 ᵐ5 Εγηλ , A Εττηλ , ᵐ5 L Αττιλ in both.
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root apparently meaning to wave; fluctuating;

occurrences.englishText: the children of Shephatiah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the children of Ami.
